gap: No result ChatGPT got says how much power the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 uses just by being switched on. CleanTechnica's 12-hour standby test lost 6% of the charge (40% to 34%) with nothing plugged in, which is about 10 W or roughly 250 Wh a day. That is about 12% of the battery every day before the fridge takes anything.
standout_why: I read three of the four cited rival pages. powersized.com/best/rv (updated 2026-10-16) gives StorageReview's 1,910 Wh usable figure for the Elite 200 V2 but no idle draw and no measured car-socket charging. solarpowerauditor.com (2026-10-06) gives the author's own bench results for usable Wh, solar watts and wall recharge time on the Elite 200 V2, DELTA 3 and Explorer 2000 v2, and says nothing measured about idle draw or 12 V charging. ecosolarkits.com has no measurements at all; its only idle figure is an unsourced '9 W at idle' for the Anker C2000 Gen 2. So usable capacity is already covered on rival pages. What none of them has is a named reviewer's idle drain or a measured car-socket charging rate, and those two numbers decide how many days a van fridge runs and how much a day of driving puts back. I could not read solargenadvisor.com (TLS certificate error), so I have not checked it.
decides: The pick stays the Elite 200 V2: two named tests put its usable capacity at 1,902–1,910 Wh, against 870–1,030 Wh for the 1 kWh alternatives. What changes is our 'fridge days' column. If the station stays on all day, the ~250 Wh/day standby drain has to come out of the budget, so 4–7 days is optimistic. Lab-measured car-socket input of about 105–108 W (the Elite 30 V2 figure) shows that charging from the 12 V socket adds only about 100 Wh per hour of driving. That supports listing EcoFlow's 800 W alternator charger as the real way to charge while driving.

unsourced: ALLPOWERS P1800: no named reviewer's measured usable capacity, idle draw or car-socket input. The search found only maker specs and an unsourced roundup claim. The IEETek P1800 result is a different product.

BLUETTI Elite 200 V2: no named reviewer measured its 12 V car-socket input (searched StorageReview, CleanTechnica, The Gadgeteer). All of them quote the 96 W / 192 W rating. The Gadgeteer's '10 W idle' is BLUETTI's claim, not a measurement.

BLUETTI AC180: no named reviewer's idle-draw or car-charging measurement. OutdoorGearLab and StorageReview don't report either; the only figures are Bluetti community forum estimates (about 15 W) and The Gadgeteer's estimate of more than 10 h to recharge from the car.
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus and DELTA 2 Max (ChatGPT's cards): no named lab measurement found within the call budget. OutdoorGearLab and solarpowerauditor tested only the base DELTA 3.
BLUETTI Elite 100 V2: Notebookcheck's review (Christian Hintze, updated 2026-10-05) measured no standby draw, usable capacity or car charging.
solargenadvisor.com (cited rival): WebFetch failed with a TLS self-signed-certificate error and the curl fallback was not approved, so I have not checked its measurements.
